summary: Client backoff jitter + streaming resume leads to out-of-order funcall ACKs and duplicate side-effects
description:
Issue summary: Customer observed duplicate external side-effects (HTTP webhook calls to their downstream job queue) after a transient networking blip during a streaming function-call session. Impact: Duplicate jobs created, downstream idempotency broken, customer had to de-duplicate resulting jobs manually for ~45 minutes. Environment: Dedicated tenant on prod us-east-1 using Go SDK v1.13.2 with default retry/backoff settings and jitter enabled. Steps to reproduce:
1) Open a streaming function-call session with a long-running tool invocation that posts to a customer webhook (their webhook acknowledges with 200 only after job is enqueued).
2) Induce a transient TCP connection interruption (short ~2s outage) between client and Redwood edge (simulated by dropping packets).
3) Client Go SDK attempts streaming resume and applies exponential backoff with jitter before reconnect.
4) On reconnect, the SDK replays buffered events; due to race between resumed ACKs from server and an in-flight webhook confirmation, two distinct funcall acceptance/ack sequences are observed by the orchestration layer. Expected behavior: At-most-once side-effect for a tool invocation when customer follows funcall confirmation pattern, or clear guidance that clients must attach idempotency tokens at tool call level. Actual behavior: Two webhook posts with different transient confirmation tokens (non-deduplicated), resulting in duplicate jobs.
Relevant logs included below and reproduced with minimal Go client sample in steps.
steps_to_reproduce: Create a streaming funcall session using Go SDK v1.13.2 and register a tool that posts to an HTTP webhook and waits for 200
Simulate a 1.5-3s network disconnect between client and the Redwood edge during the funcall response streaming
Allow client SDK to auto-reconnect using default backoff+jitter
Observe webhook logs: two separate POSTs within 1-4s window for the same logical funcall id

comments: 2026-03-12 - Maya Patel (support): Initial report received from customer via support form, attached webhook logs and short tcpdump.
2026-03-12 - SRE (Riley Thompson): Confirmed transient packet drops seen on edge host edge-32 in us-east-1; serving-runtime reported resume handshake succeeded twice for same stream id.

2026-03-13 - Eng (Ethan Chen): Reproduced locally with Go SDK; hypothesis: ACK race between server-side funcall confirmation and client-side replay when jittered reconnect causes duplicated confirmation path.
2026-03-14 - Customer (Vectorly Analytics) via CS: Requested mitigation guidance and whether Redwood can enforce stricter at-most-once semantics for funcall tool side-effects.
2026-03-14 - Ethan Chen (assignee): Requested additional traces (full tcpdump + server-side trace) and asked customer to try client-side per-funcall idempotency token as temporary mitigation.
investigation_notes: Reproducer: local cluster test replicated duplicate POSTs when client jitter value > 300ms and server-side delayed webhook confirmation occurred during reconnect window.

Findings: Server will accept a resumed stream and re-emit pending funcall events; if the original funcall was already delivered to the tool, and tool's confirmation path is not tied to a stable idempotency token, downstreams will see duplicate side-effects.

Root cause hypothesis: Combination of (1) streaming replay semantics that re-queue pending funcall deliverables on resume, (2) client-side jittered reconnect that causes slightly different sequencing of ACKs/confirmations, and (3) lack of enforced funcall-level idempotency token by the platform for legacy tool integrations.
Edge host network glitch correlated with restart of connection worker; serving-runtime accepted new session and re-sent buffered ops without marking them as 'replay' in webhook payload headers.
Related: SUP-41209 had similar webhook duplicate symptom but in that case header mapping was the trigger; here it's replay ordering + missing idempotency token.
resolution: Workaround provided: recommend customer add a strong idempotency key in the tool payload (X-Vectorly-Job-Id or similar) and make downstream webhook idempotent. Short-term change: Go SDK patch to include per-funcall idempotency token by default on replay (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-go/pull/512) — roll forward in canary today in us-east-1. Long-term: platform change to annotate replayed funcall events with 'X-Redwood-Replay: true' header and emit durable funcall id to allow automatic dedupe in edge and in tooling. Tracking engineering epic: ENG-STREAM-2026.
follow_up_tasks: ENG: Add replay flag header and durable funcall id in serving-runtime (assigned ENG-STREAM-2026)
SDK: backport default per-funcall idempotency token to v1.13.x and v1.14 (PRs created)
SRE: add alert to detect >1 external POSTs for same funcall id within 10s window on edge hosts
